title: Etale locality and base change of coarse-morphism properties
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, stacks in groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be any morphism of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$, and let $\{W_i\to\mathcal B\}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of representable etale maps from schemes. A morphism of stacks is separated when its relative diagonal is proper, with properness tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It is quasi-compact when, after every scheme base change $T$ into its target, inverse images of quasi-compact opens of $T$ have quasi-compact underlying point spaces. It is a universal homeomorphism when every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism on underlying point spaces. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The underlying points are field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. For each property $P$ in the list separated, quasi-compact, universal homeomorphism, $f$ has $P$ if and only if every base change $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}W_i\to W_i$ has $P$. Each of these three properties is preserved under arbitrary base change by a Deligne--Mumford stack. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts.

Family version by scheme coproduct. Restricted to DM source and target; universal homeomorphisms still tested by arbitrary algebraic stacks.

proof.text: We first record the point calculation used below. For arbitrary maps $X\to Y$, $Z\to Y$ of the stacks in question, a pair of point classes with the same image in $|Y|$ has representatives over fields whose images become isomorphic over a common extension. Over that extension the representatives and this isomorphism form an object of $X\times_Y Z$. Thus $|X\times_Y Z|\to|X|\times_{|Y|}|Z|$ is surjective. In particular images pull back as sets, and jointly surjective families remain jointly surjective after base change. This uses no assertion that this map of point sets is injective. The objectwise triple construction is the specified 2-fibre product.

Put $D=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$. For any $\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$, put $\mathcal A'=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B'$. Then $D'=\mathcal A'\times_{\mathcal B'}\mathcal A'$ identifies with $D\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B'$, and $\Delta_{f'}$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along $D'\to D$. Indeed a test object of $D'$ is two objects of $\mathcal A$ with an isomorphism of their images, together with one compatible object of $\mathcal B'$; the fibre of its diagonal is the space of isomorphisms between those two objects inducing the specified isomorphism in $\mathcal B$. This is exactly the fibre of $\Delta_f$ at the underlying object of $D$. These identifications commute with arrows and pullbacks. The relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces: on any scheme test its fibre is the subfunctor of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A}(a_1,a_2)$ mapping to the specified section of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal B}(f(a_1),f(a_2))$. Both Isom functors are algebraic spaces, and taking this fibre is an algebraic-space fibre product.

If $f$ is separated, every scheme test of $\Delta_{f'}$ is, by Step 2, a base change of a scheme test of $\Delta_f$ (take its composite into $D$). Properness of algebraic-space morphisms is stable under arbitrary algebraic-space base change. Consequently that test is proper, proving separatedness of $f'$. In particular separatedness implies separatedness of each $f_i$. Conversely suppose every $f_i$ is separated. Fix a scheme $T\to D$. The algebraic spaces $E_i=T\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$ form a jointly surjective etale family over $T$ by Step 1 and the chart calculus. Choose surjective etale scheme atlases $Q_i\to E_i$. Then $\{Q_i\to T\}$ is jointly surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, hence an fppf covering. The algebraic space $H=T\times_D\mathcal A$ has proper pullback over every $Q_i$: the map $Q_i\to D$ lifts to $D\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$, so its pullback of $\Delta_f$ is a test of $\Delta_{f_i}$ by Step 2. Properness descends along this scheme fppf covering, giving properness of $H\to T$. Every scheme test has now been checked, so $f$ is separated.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness is preserved under base change directly from the stated scheme-test definition. Given $\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$, a scheme $T\to\mathcal B'$ and a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$, the inverse image of $V$ under $\mathcal A'\times_{\mathcal B'}T\to T$ is the same stack as $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V$ via the composite $V\to\mathcal B$; both are 2-fibre products of DM stacks, hence DM stacks with etale scheme atlases, so the point topology applies. Their point spaces agree with their atlas topologies. The latter is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $f$. This also proves the forward implication for each $W_i$.

source.place: Tag 050V (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), omitted proof expanded for the item's scheme-test convention

proof.text: Suppose each $f_i$ is quasi-compact. Fix a scheme $T\to\mathcal B$ and a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$. Choose etale scheme atlases of the algebraic spaces $W_i\times_{\mathcal B}V$, and cover their source schemes by affine opens $U_{ia}$. The maps $U_{ia}\to V$ are etale, flat and locally finitely presented by the chart calculus. They are open on point spaces, and their images cover $|V|$ by Step 1. Quasi-compactness of $V$ supplies finitely many of these images covering $V$. Every selected $U_{ia}$ is quasi-compact, since an affine scheme is a spectrum and spectra are quasi-compact. This selection requires neither quasi-compactness of a whole $W_i$ nor any condition on intersections of affine opens.

source.place: Tag 0DTL (lemma-check-quasi-compact-covering), finite quasi-compact scheme refinement in its proof; algebra.tex Tag 00E8

proof.text: For each of the finitely selected $U=U_{ia}$, its map to $\mathcal B$ factors through $W_i$. The hypothesis on $f_i$, tested on the scheme $U\to W_i$ and its quasi-compact open $U$ itself, says that $|\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}U|$ is quasi-compact. Its map to $|\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V|$ is continuous. These finitely many point images cover the latter by Step 1. Given any open cover of that latter space, its inverse image on each of the finitely many quasi-compact sources has a finite subcover; the union of these finite choices covers every point of the target. Thus $|\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V|$ is quasi-compact. This holds for every $T,V$, and proves quasi-compactness of $f$. All products of DM stacks used here are DM and have scheme atlases.

source.place: Tag 0DTL (lemma-check-quasi-compact-covering), final surjective-image argument, written directly for scheme tests

proof.text: For universal homeomorphisms the base-change implication is also formal: if $f$ has the property and $\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ is a DM base change, every algebraic-stack test $Z\to\mathcal B'$ gives $(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B')\times_{\mathcal B'}Z\simeq\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}Z$ over $Z$. Hence the point map is a homeomorphism. Conversely assume every $f_i$ is a universal homeomorphism and fix an arbitrary algebraic stack $Z\to\mathcal B$. The stacks $Z_i=Z\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$ are algebraic; choose smooth surjective scheme atlases $U_i\to Z_i$. Their composites $q_i:U_i\to Z$ are representable smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented, and jointly surjective by Step 1. Thus each $|q_i|$ is open. Write $X=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}Z$ and $X_i=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}U_i=X\times_ZU_i$. Because $U_i\to\mathcal B$ factors through $W_i$, the hypothesis on $f_i$ says $h_i:|X_i|\to|U_i|$ is a homeomorphism. No DM assumption on $Z$ or $Z_i$ is made.

Let $h:|X|\to|Z|$. It is continuous. For any $z\in|Z|$, choose $u\in|U_i|$ above it. The unique point of $|X_i|$ above $u$ supplies a point of $|X|$ above $z$, proving surjectivity. If $x_1,x_2\in|X|$ both map to $z$, Step 1 lifts each pair $(x_j,u)$ to a point $t_j\in|X_i|$. Injectivity of $h_i$ gives $t_1=t_2$, and projection gives $x_1=x_2$. Finally for an open $O\subseteq|X|$, its inverse image $O_i\subseteq|X_i|$ is open. Each $h_i(O_i)$ is open in $|U_i|$, so $|q_i|(h_i(O_i))$ is open in $|Z|$. Their union is $h(O)$: one containment follows from commutativity, and the other follows by lifting the pair $(x,u)$ for any $x\in O$. Hence $h$ is open, continuous and bijective, and therefore a homeomorphism. Since $Z$ was an arbitrary algebraic-stack test, $f$ is a universal homeomorphism. This completes all three equivalences and all base-change clauses.
